title: Consequences of linear-time Orthogonal Vectors
formal:
Does essentially-linear deterministic time for Orthogonal Vectors in every fixed polylogarithmic dimension regime imply failure of the Exponential Time Hypothesis? With \(\mathsf{EL}_{\mathrm{OV}}\) and \(\mathsf{ETH}\) defined below, the proposition is
\[
\mathsf{EL}_{\mathrm{OV}}\ \Longrightarrow\ \neg\mathsf{ETH}.
\]
Equivalently, does \(\mathsf{ETH}\) imply that some such dimension regime lacks deterministic \(O(N^{1+\varepsilon})\)-time algorithms for at least one \(\varepsilon>0\)? Here \(N\) is the complete binary input length. The target is a logical implication about algorithm existence, not a request to assume that the premise already holds. The explicit dimension quantifiers and binary encodings below complete the source's informal polylogarithmic-dimension formulation, while retaining its deterministic multitape Turing-machine model.

source_formulation.text: Furthermore, we do not know if the existence of an essentially-linear time algorithm for OVP would imply that ETH is false.
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 3

why: A proof would base some polynomial-time hardness on ETH rather than the stronger SETH assumption, clarifying how much exponential hardness is needed for a widely used fine-grained benchmark. A refutation would expose a substantive separation between these algorithmic barriers. The importance lies in the relationship between two major hypotheses, beyond an improvement to one OV algorithm.
status_note: The STACS 2022 source explicitly asks this OV-to-ETH implication in Remark 1. A bounded primary-source review through 16 September 2026 checked the source’s latest recorded preprint version, the authors’ subsequent guessing paper and selected 2024–2026 OV/circuit and low-dimensional algorithm results, finding no verified resolution. Source-open status is dated and qualified, not an exhaustive present-day certificate. The exact polylogarithmic promise family, encodings and finite-alphabet details are disclosed editorial completions of the source’s deterministic Turing-machine setting.

progress.text: The STACS source explicitly leaves the OV-to-ETH implication open in Remark 1 while proving an analogous implication for log-CircuitSAT in Theorem 22.

The authors’ later journal work studies deterministic-to-nondeterministic speedups and SAT in nondeterministic linear time. Its main implications do not establish the OV-to-deterministic-ETH statement.
Williams relates OV algorithms and hardness to nonuniform circuit lower bounds and SETH. These are distinct consequences from falsifying ETH.
Alman and Li state a deterministic \(\widetilde O(n\,1.155^{d})\)-time OV algorithm in Theorem 1.3, improving the exponential dependence on dimension.

The ICALP paper of Dürr, Kipouridis, Lampis and Węgrzycki gives further low-dimensional and multi-list OV results; its introductory hardness statements concern SETH and Set Cover, not the target ETH implication.

Individual review recovered the source’s time and machine conventions, made the implication and its full negation explicit, and checked selected later primary papers without finding a resolution of this precise implication.

category_assignment.reason: The implication compares Orthogonal Vectors running time directly with ETH.

importance.reason: A substantial foundational implication linking ETH to a central problem behind fine-grained lower bounds. Resolving it would clarify whether very strong OV speedups already undermine the weaker exponential-time assumption. Its broad consequence justifies high importance, while the precisely selected near-linear and Turing-machine regime is narrower than the full OV hypothesis.

sentences: Orthogonal Vectors asks whether two lists of Boolean vectors contain a pair with no coordinate equal to one in both vectors.
The premise asks for deterministic essentially-linear algorithms in every fixed polylogarithmic dimension regime.
The question is whether that premise forces the Exponential Time Hypothesis to fail.
Known implications to the stronger SETH assumption and recent low-dimensional algorithms do not settle this precise target.
A complete answer must prove the implication or establish both its algorithmic premise and ETH as the full negation.

definitions:
All logarithms have base two. An Orthogonal Vectors instance consists of integers \(n\ge2\), \(d\ge1\), and two ordered lists \(A=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\), \(B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)\) with \(a_i,b_j\in\{0,1\}^{d}\). Repeated vectors and zero vectors are allowed. The answer is yes exactly when
\[
\exists i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\quad
\sum_{h=1}^{d}a_{i,h}b_{j,h}=0.
\]
The sum is over the integers, not modulo two. Thus no coordinate may be one in both selected vectors. Both lists are explicitly present; there is no succinct input, preprocessing phase, online sequence of queries, or promise on vector weights.

For a nonnegative integer \(r\), let \(\operatorname{bin}(r+1)\) be its usual binary representation without leading zeroes, put \(\ell(r)=|\operatorname{bin}(r+1)|\), and encode it by \(\operatorname{code}(r)=1^{\ell(r)}0\operatorname{bin}(r+1)\). An OV encoding is \(\operatorname{code}(n)\operatorname{code}(d)\), followed by the \(nd\) coordinate bits of \(A\) in list order and then those of \(B\). There is no padding or trailing data. Its length is denoted by \(N\).

For each fixed integer \(b\ge1\), the promised domain \(\mathcal I_b\) consists of these valid encodings satisfying
\[
d\le\bigl\lceil\log_2(n+2)\bigr\rceil^{b}.
\]
This specifies the family of polylogarithmic regimes, rather than selecting a single low-dimensional constant or allowing arbitrary polynomial dimension. The essentially-linear premise means
\[
\mathsf{EL}_{\mathrm{OV}}:\quad
\forall b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \forall\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\
\exists M\ \exists C\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\
\forall z\in\mathcal I_b:\quad
M(z)\text{ returns the correct OV answer in at most }
C(|z|+1)^{1+\varepsilon}\text{ steps}.
\]
The program and constant may depend on \(b,\varepsilon\), but not on the input. No correctness or time requirement is imposed outside the promised domain. Every positive rational overhead exponent is required; one fixed \(1+\varepsilon\) bound does not establish the premise. Nor is one algorithm with a single subpolynomial overhead demanded. For each fixed \(b\), the explicit length is \(n\) times a polylogarithmic factor, so using \(n\) instead of \(N\) gives the same family of essentially-linear bounds after changing \(\varepsilon\).

A 3-CNF instance consists of \(v\ge0\) named Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_v\) and an ordered list of \(m\ge0\) clauses, each an ordered list of at most three literals. A literal is \(x_i\) or \(\neg x_i\) for \(1\le i\le v\); repeated literals and clauses are allowed. A formula is satisfied when each clause has a true literal. The empty conjunction is true and an empty clause is false. An assignment gives a bit to each of the \(v\) variables. Its binary encoding is \(\operatorname{code}(v)\operatorname{code}(m)\), followed for each clause by its encoded length and then its literals, each represented by a sign bit followed by \(\operatorname{code}(i)\); sign zero denotes a positive literal. There are no extra bits. Write \(L\) for this encoding length and \(v(F)\) for its declared number of variables, including unused ones.

For \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\), define \(\mathsf{SATFast}(\delta)\) to mean that there exist a deterministic machine \(S\) and integers \(C\ge1\), \(k\ge0\), such that on every valid encoded 3-CNF formula \(F\), \(S\) decides satisfiability correctly and halts within
\[
C(L+1)^k\,2^{\delta v(F)}
\]
steps. The clock is worst case, and the constants and program may depend on \(\delta\). Invalid formula encodings are outside this domain. The Exponential Time Hypothesis used here is precisely
\[
\mathsf{ETH}:\quad
\exists\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\;\neg\mathsf{SATFast}(\delta).
\]
Its failure is \(\forall\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\;\mathsf{SATFast}(\delta)\). This definition does not silently exchange the order of the algorithm and exponent quantifiers, or replace ETH by its stronger variant concerning every clause width.

All machines in both definitions are ordinary deterministic multitape Turing machines with finitely many states and a fixed finite positive number of two-way infinite tapes. The alphabet is \(\{0,1,\#,\square\}\), with \(\square\) blank. The binary input occupies consecutive cells of the first tape beginning at zero; every other cell starts blank, and every head starts at zero. All tapes, including the input tape, are writable. In one transition the machine reads one symbol per tape, writes one per tape, moves each head by at most one cell, and changes state. An accepting or rejecting halting state returns the answer. Every transition costs one step. There is no randomness, advice, oracle, random-access instruction or parallel primitive. Each program is uniform over its input lengths, even though different fixed exponents may have different programs. These are standard finite-alphabet refinements of the model in Section 3.1 of the source.
answer_criterion:
Supply a complete, mathematically correct Lean proof of \(\mathsf{EL}_{\mathrm{OV}}\Rightarrow\neg\mathsf{ETH}\), or of its full logical negation
\[
\mathsf{EL}_{\mathrm{OV}}\ \land\ \mathsf{ETH}.
\]
A positive proof must respect all input, dimension, machine and exponent quantifiers in the two definitions. It may establish the implication by any valid mathematical argument; no particular reduction format or uniform compiler between algorithms is imposed. For a negative answer it is necessary to prove both essentially-linear OV algorithms in every specified regime and an ETH lower bound: a faster OV algorithm alone, a failure of one proposed reduction, or an oracle-relative separation is insufficient. Likewise, merely deriving failure of SETH or a \(2^{c v}\) SAT algorithm for one fixed \(c>0\) does not prove failure of ETH. A randomized algorithm, an algorithm only for a fixed small multiple of logarithmic dimension, or a fixed truly subquadratic OV bound does not meet the full premise. No Lean formalization is claimed by this review.

context_blocks.text: The question compares two central sources of conditional lower bounds. Orthogonal Vectors is a polynomial-time problem used to transfer fine-grained hardness to many algorithmic tasks. ETH instead asserts an exponential-time obstruction for 3-CNF satisfiability.

The source defines essentially-linear time by having \(O(N^{1+\varepsilon})\) decision algorithms for every fixed positive \(\varepsilon\). This includes a family of algorithms with different exponents; it does not mean exact linear time or only linear time times a fixed power of a logarithm.

Its main ETH implication concerns log-CircuitSAT, a restricted circuit-satisfiability problem. Remark 1 separately asks the OV implication. The log-CircuitSAT theorem cannot be reported as already resolving this different target.

Later work continues to connect faster OV algorithms to SETH and to nonuniform circuit lower bounds. Those conclusions address other assumptions or resources and do not by themselves establish the ETH implication.

Recent low-dimensional algorithms improve the dependence on dimension in their respective source models, including a deterministic \(\widetilde O(n\,1.155^{d})\) bound. An exponential factor in \(d\) does not supply the required essentially-linear algorithm throughout every fixed polylogarithmic dimension regime.

The exact list representation, dimension-exponent family and finite-alphabet conventions are explicit editorial completions. The original question does not spell them out, and its separate discussion of random-access machines makes it especially important to retain the chosen Turing-machine setting.

checked_sources: Read the full canonical record and actual STACS2022 article55 PDF, pp2–3 for the source question, p6 for DTIME’s writable-input multitape model, and pp12–13 for Theorem22 and Question26. Publisher metadata gives 9March2022, not the conference’s 15March opening date or misleading recent crawler timestamps. arXiv2008.06805 history lists v1 August2020 through v5 23January2022 and no later version.

The source defines essentially-linear as membership in O(N^(1+epsilon)) for every positive epsilon, not a single O(N polylogN) algorithm. The card therefore quantifies separately over algorithms for each rational epsilon and fixed dimension exponent b. Rational exponents suffice by monotonicity. All polynomial-logarithmic dimension bounds with fixed multiplicative constants are covered by a higher integer b beyond finitely many small n; n+2 avoids boundary issues. Exact promise-family encoding is an explicitly disclosed editorial completion, not a verbatim source theorem.

Used the standard two-list, integer-inner-product-zero OV definition, confirmed directly in ICALP2026 Definition1.1 and Alman–Li Section1.6. Repetitions do not affect decision existence. For fixed b the binary length N=2nd+O(logn+logd), so switching n versus full input length preserves the for-every-positive-exponent notion. Did not substitute arbitrary polynomial dimension, online indexing, parity orthogonality, randomized success or a single fixed d=c logn regime.

ETH is copied in its precise source quantifier sense: some positive delta precludes all deterministic 3SAT algorithms with poly(L)2^(delta v) running time. Failure gives an algorithm for each delta, with its polynomial exponent allowed to depend on delta. The card does not silently infer one uniform 2^o(v) algorithm. The implication’s full negation requires both EL_OV and ETH, not merely proving the antecedent or showing one reduction fails.
